I don't understand the UK govt's "Eat Out to Help Out" restaurant subsidy.
Weirdly it doesn't cover the safest option: takeaway.
Eating in restaurants and bars seems very poor value, in terms of $ of GDP generated for each additional person who catches COVID19. 1/2

author: MrinankSharma
text: @dishwash_expert @holmenkollin @GidMK In the countries we considered (mostly European), mask wearing was never the first NPI activated.

author: MrinankSharma
text: @dishwash_expert @holmenkollin @GidMK Sorry I didn't explain that so well. NPI1 is the first NPI that was activated (and so on). This can be different interventions in different countries.  We wanted to test whether the model was just inferring that the earliest interventions are always more effective.

author: MrinankSharma
text:
@GidMK We also test sensitivity to the specific structural assumptions that the model makes, and again find low sensitivity. 

Thanks again for the review! Happy to take feedback and discuss more :) 5/

author: MrinankSharma
text: @GidMK One of the strengths of the paper is the extensive sensitivity analysis performed including: changing epidemiological parameters (such as the base reproduction number, generational interval), countries included and more ... 4/

author: MrinankSharma
text:
@GidMK Our NPI dataset and modelling code is available here: https://t.co/5ONUXfknNA 

We're really excited to see how other people use it! 3/

author: MrinankSharma
text:
@GidMK We attempt to investigate the effect of unobserved factors by including interventions from the OxCGRT dataset and running the model when excluding some interventions that we collected ourselves. 

The low sensitivity increases our confidence in the effectiveness estimates 2/ https://t.co/hhfKnXkOpA

author: MrinankSharma
text:
@GidMK Thanks for the review (I'm one of authors)! 

Absolutely correct that it is hard to infer causation here, especially as the data we have is observational. 1/

author: MrinankSharma
text: @holmenkollin @GidMK One of the authors here. We actually did a sensitivity test where we just looked at the order that different interventions were implemented. We don't always find that the earlier interventions are the most effective. (Plot is in the appendix of the paper). https://t.co/qUXjzCUjAh

text: @sorenmind @MickMills @jussisaramo @Babak_Javid_Lab @yeewhye @biomonika @AlexCrane33 In particular, data from Spain, when mask wearing, to our knowledge, began during lockdown has a surprisingly big effect. author: MrinankSharma
text: @sorenmind @MickMills @jussisaramo @Babak_Javid_Lab @yeewhye @biomonika @AlexCrane33  Here is an additional plot showing sensitivity over leaving out individual countries, but for all countries (one-by-one). Given we have the least data for masks, it is one of the more sensitive results. 1/ https://t.co/Zta1JJwdbO

author: MrinankSharma
text: @MickMills @jussisaramo @sorenmind @Babak_Javid_Lab @yeewhye In general, we selected countries based on thresholding on the number of cases (at the time of modelling), the availability of NPI data (at the time of modelling) and how trustworthy we estimated the reporting of deaths to be.

author: MrinankSharma
text: @MickMills @jussisaramo @sorenmind @Babak_Javid_Lab @yeewhye We excluded South Korea because they made heavy use of contact tracing, something that we didn't model because data on contact tracing is very difficult to get. We're looking into using more countries, but collecting high quality data takes some time. (more details below).

author: MrinankSharma
text: Furthermore, we performed 15 sensitivity analyses and evaluated predictions on unseen data. We found strong support for our conclusions, suggesting that they are robust.  9/8

author: MrinankSharma
text:
We find:
1⃣Schools may play a surprisingly large role in #COVID19 transmission. 
2⃣Testing, closing high-risk businesses and limiting gathering sizes are effective at reducing transmission whilst imposing low burden. 
5/8

author: MrinankSharma
text: We additionally estimate the burden imposed on individuals of different NPIs, performing an online survey of preferences and using the MaxDiff method. 4/8 https://t.co/VPxMj7YojJ

author: MrinankSharma
text: We develop a novel semi-mechanistic Bayesian model using *both* confirmed cases and fatalities as observations, allowing us to leverage significantly more countries than previous work. Our model makes sensible predictions on held-out countries. 3/8 https://t.co/nWI0qlI5cS

author: MrinankSharma
text: Countries implemented different NPIs in different orders (and in different points in time), allowing us to estimate the effect of individual interventions. We have collected and publicly released a high-quality, NPI intervention dataset, which was subject to fact checking. 2/8 https://t.co/FKR1K7nVTn

author: MrinankSharma
text:
Really excited to share our new preprint modelling the effectiveness and surveying the burden of 9 different non-pharmaceutical interventions against #COVID19 transmission, using data collected across 41 different countries.

This is crazy. On 16/3, experts asked to forecast US COVID-19 cases come 29/3.
Only 3 of 18 had the right answer anywhere near their 80% confidence interval.
OK, was the outcome (123k) a surprising one? No!
A simple-as-hell exponential growth extrapolation forecast ~130k!
1/2
